textbookText: For many years, people didn't have any idea where modern humans, Homo sapiens sapiens, came from. Many anthropologists believe that modern humans might have evolved from primitive eutherian mammals during the cretaceous period. These early mammals were terrestrial, insect-eating, and shrew-like. They were the ancestors from which other mammal species evolved. Among these mammals, the first primates, resembling present-day treeshrews, evolved during the Paleocene epoch of the tertiary period in the Cenozoic era. Primates further evolved into two suborders: Prosimii and Anthropoidea. Among them Prosimians include some animals such as Tree-shrews, Lemurs, Tarsiers etc. Evolution of modern human from anthropoid ancestry is outlined in the chart given below:

Figure: 7.4.1 Flowchart of Human evolution Platyrrhini or new world monkeys had primitive dentition similar to prosimians. They had flat noses with widely separated nostrils, long prehensile tails, and did not use their limbs for grasping. Catarrhini or old world monkeys had dentition more similar to humans than prosimians. They had narrow noses with closely placed and downward nostrils, short nonprehensile tails, and used their limbs to grasp. Catarrhini diverged into two groups:

Cercopithecoidea (old world monkey) and Hominoidea (ape and man). Hominoidea further evolved into 3 families in the Miocene epoch of Tertiary period in Cenozoic era, viz. Hyalobatidae, Pongidae and Hominida. The first two families constitute apes of various sizes such as Gibbon, Gorilla, chimpanzee, etc. Whereas, the Hominids are believed to be the ancestor of humans as they have some characteristics like erect body posture, long and stout hind limbs, bipedalism, mostly terrestrial, well-developed brain, etc.

Thomas Huxley in his study claimed humans to have a very close relationship with apes. He even concluded in his book 'Man's Place in Nature' (1863) that humans might have evolved from apes. It was further supported by Charles Darwin (1871) in his book 'Descent of Man' (1871). Later, a pre-human fossil was discovered after 1925 showed it to be around 2 million years old suggesting all primates like monkeys, apes and humans share a common ancestor. Now, scientists agree that humans originated in central Asia around 24-36 million years ago from some sort of ape-like ancestor.

7.4.3 APES AND MAN Human beings and ape have the following similar characteristics: There exists a close relationship between apes and man some of which are listed below: i. Both lack a tail. ii. Both bear larger brains, cranial cavity and efficient memory. iii. Both exhibit prominent brow ridges above the eyes. iv. Both can communicate by producing sounds by vocal means. v. Both have highly developed facial musculature to express emotion/feelings such as anger, surprise, pleasure and laughter using facial gestures. vi. Both have a tendency to live as couples. In fact, females undergo periodic menstruation. These resemblance shown by apes and men, suggests them to be 'cousins' descended from common ancestors.
